tickets.title: The 'Ghost' Website
tickets.summary: A marketing user says 'site-beta.local' is showing an old version of the page. You updated the DNS record to 10.0.0.100, but their machine keeps hitting 10.0.0.20.

triage.q: If Nslookup (direct query) is correct, but Ping (OS resolution) is wrong, where is the false information likely coming from?
options: A local override on the client machine

diagnosis.q: Which local file or cache is checked by the OS before it even asks the DNS server?

fix.q: How do you ensure the client uses the global DNS record instead of the local override?
options: Clear the Hosts file and run 'ipconfig /flushdns'

debrief.summary: The 'Hosts' file has absolute priority. If a developer or tech left an entry there, the PC will ignore the real DNS server.
debrief.takeaway: Compare nslookup results against ping results to detect local resolution overrides.

tickets.title: Intermittent App Failures
tickets.summary: An internal app works for some users but fails for others. You find that the hostname 'app-srv' resolves to two different IPs, but one of those servers was decommissioned months ago.
artifact: Server Inventory: 10.10.1.22 was retired in November
DNS Console: Record for 10.10.1.22 has a timestamp from 4 months ago

triage.q: Why are some users failing while others succeed?
options: The DNS server is load balancing (Round Robin) between a working and a non-existent IP
The retired server is still partially online
The app requires a specific MAC address

diagnosis.q: Why did the DNS record for the retired server stay in the database after the server was shut down?
options: The server didn't have 'Register in DNS' checked
Aging and Scavenging is likely disabled or not configured correctly

fix.q: How do you clean up this record and prevent similar 'ghost' records in the future?
options: Delete the record manually and enable 'Scavenging' on the server and zone

debrief.summary: DNS records for dynamically assigned IPs or decommissioned servers will persist forever unless Scavenging is enabled.
debrief.takeaway: Scavenging automates the deletion of 'stale' records based on their timestamp.

tickets.title: Domain Login Delay
tickets.summary: Users report that logging into their computers takes 5 minutes. They can ping the Domain Controller by name, but AD-specific tools are failing.
artifact: DNS Manager: The '_msdcs' folder is missing or empty

triage.q: Since ping works but AD discovery fails, what specific type of DNS record is missing?

diagnosis.q: Which service on the Domain Controller is responsible for registering these vital SRV records into DNS?

fix.q: What is the fastest way to force the Domain Controller to re-register its missing service records?
options: Restart the 'Netlogon' service on the Domain Controller
Rejoin the client to the domain

debrief.summary: Active Directory cannot function without SRV records. They tell clients exactly which servers handle LDAP, Kerberos, and GC requests.
debrief.takeaway: Ping only proves the 'A' record exists. SRV records are the 'map' for AD services.

tickets.title: Local Resolution Only
tickets.summary: Users can reach internal servers (filesrv, intranet), but they cannot reach google.com or any external websites.

triage.q: If internal names work but external names fail, where is the breakdown in the DNS search process?
options: The DNS server doesn't know where to send queries for zones it doesn't host
The ISP is blocking all DNS traffic

diagnosis.q: What configuration tells a local DNS server to 'ask' an external server (like 8.8.8.8) if it cannot find the answer locally?

fix.q: How do you enable the DNS server to resolve external internet addresses?
options: Add a public DNS IP (e.g., 8.8.8.8) to the 'Forwarders' tab in Server Properties
Enable 'Dynamic Updates' on the internal zone
Create an 'A' record for google.com manually
Add a new NIC to the server

debrief.summary: DNS Forwarders are a speed and security optimization. They send all non-local queries to a trusted external resolver.
debrief.takeaway: Without Forwarders or working Root Hints, an internal DNS server is an island.
